page: Amazon Web Services f2.12xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is configured at 512 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, offering 10.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes equipped with 1880 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, and two integrated Xilinx Virtex UltraScale+ (VU47P) hardware accelerators providing 160 GB of combined accelerator memory.

CPU benchmark results demonstrate strong performance across compute and cryptographic operations. In stress-ng testing, both single-core (2993.25) and multi-core (71813.3) scores rank in the top 25 percent. Passmark testing similarly places the instance in the top quartile for overall CPU score (56429.21) and encryption throughput (56862.73). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 236.54 GB/sec, while Geekbench ray tracing and image processing register in the top 25 percent. General system memory bandwidth tests show moderate throughput, yielding 105.97 GB/sec on uncached reads and 58.55 GB/sec on uncached writes.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge in host-based machine learning inference. Processing 70B parameter models purely on the CPU yields poor text generation throughput at 2.34 tokens/sec, demonstrating that the system architecture relies on offloading target workloads to the dedicated FPGAs rather than the general-purpose CPU cores. Given its balanced resource footprint of high-capacity memory, local high-speed NVMe storage, and programmable logic, this server is suitable for FPGA development, financial analytics, hardware-accelerated genomics pipelines, real-time video processing, and data compression workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services f2.12xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 3.4 GHz, 512 GB of DDR4 system memory, a bundled 1880 GB NVMe SSD, and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. For hardware acceleration, it integrates two Xilinx Virtex UltraScale+ VU47P FPGA devices offering 160 GB of combined accelerator memory. Benchmark results indicate top-tier CPU performance in stress-ng and Passmark multi-core testing, alongside strong encryption and multi-threaded decompression throughput. While raw host-CPU large-model LLM generation exhibits lower throughput, the instance is architectured to offload compute-intensive kernels directly to programmable hardware logic. This setup fits custom FPGA-accelerated workloads, high-frequency financial modeling, genomics analysis, video transcoding, and memory-dense data pipelines requiring high-speed local NVMe storage.
